# Catukkanipāta (AN 4)
**ID:** AN 4

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Catukkanipāta* (AN 4), or "The Book of the Fours," constitutes the fourth major division of the *Aṅguttaranikāya* in the Sutta Piṭaka, grouping discourses that systematically expound the Dhamma through numerical sets of four [SuttaCentral]. The nipāta covers a wide array of doctrinal topics, meditative practices, and social interactions. Individual suttas treat subjects such as the attainment of the four jhānas and subsequent rebirth in the form and formless realms (*rūpabhava* and *arūpabhava*) [Bodhi 1970; Polak 2011], classifications of ascetics and stages of awakening [Wen; Polak 2011], lay ethics such as freedom from debt in the *Anaṇyasutta* (AN 4.62) [Stanley et al. 2018], and the ethical demythologizing of Vedic animal sacrifice in the *Ujjayasutta* (AN 4.39) [Ham 2016]. Narrative contexts in the collection also feature prominent disciples; for example, Ānanda instructs and pardons an ailing nun in the *Bhikkhunīsutta* (AN 4.159), Sāriputta describes his mastery of analytical knowledges (*paṭisambhidā-ñāṇa*) in AN 4.173, and the *Yuganaddhasutta* (AN 4.170) outlines liberation achieved through the tandem cultivation of tranquility (*samatha*) and insight (*vipassanā*) [Nyanaponika et al. 2003; Culadasa and Immergut 2011].
SuttaCentral records full parallels across various canonical traditions, including 27 in the *Saṃyuktāgama* (SĀ), 10 in the *Ekottarikāgama* (EĀ), and others in the *Madhyamāgama* (MĀ), Sanskrit works like the *Arthaviniścayasūtra*, and Central Asian manuscript fragments [SuttaCentral]. Several specific discourses show significant cross-canonical witness: the *Doṇasutta* (AN 4.36) parallels Chinese *Saṃyuktāgama* discourses (SĀ 101, SĀ² 267) as well as a British Library Gāndhārī Kharoṣṭhī fragment [SuttaCentral; Anālayo 2017], while the account of the Buddha's four marvels in AN 4.127 shares thematic parallels with MN 123 and MĀ 32 [Anālayo 2011]. DharmaNexus detects extensive text reuse within the Pali Canon (over 105,000 matches), aligning substantial shared passages with adjacent *Aṅguttaranikāya* nipātas (AN 5, AN 3, AN 10) and the *Catukkapuggalapaññatti* (Pp 2.4), alongside cross-language alignments with Sanskrit and Tibetan treatises such as the *Arthaviniścayasūtra*, the *Śrāvakabhūmi*, and Śamathadeva's *Abhidharmakośaṭīkopayikā* [DharmaNexus]. Both SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus corroborate alignments with the *Arthaviniścayasūtra* and the *Saṃyuktāgama* [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].
